evals.prompt: Crea un monorepo para la empresa acme con una web en Next.js y una API en NestJS. Somos un solo equipo y queremos compartir las validaciones entre front y back.
evals.expected_output: The agent picks zod mode and justifies it with the matrix, runs scaffold-monorepo.mjs --scope acme --contracts zod first with --dry-run and then without it after confirmation. It does not run create-next-app or nest new without permission. It explains how to connect the apps with scaffold-app.mjs (the @acme/tsconfig extends, oxc-config, workspace:* dependencies) and finishes by verifying with pnpm turbo run lint typecheck test build and pnpm check:boundaries. The reply is in Spanish.
assertions: Chooses zod mode and justifies it
Does not run create-next-app or nest new without permission
Verifies with turbo run and pnpm check:boundaries

evals.prompt: In my monorepo (it already has packages/contracts, apps/web, apps/api and apps/mobile) add the invoices domain end to end for all three clients.
evals.expected_output: The agent runs scaffold-fullstack-feature.mjs invoice --targets api,web,mobile with --dry-run and then without it. Result: packages/contracts/src/invoices with the Zod schema and './invoices' in exports; the 18 nestjs-architecture files in apps/api/src/modules/invoices; the nextjs-architecture feature in apps/web/src/features/invoices; the react-native-architecture feature in apps/mobile/src/features/invoices; workspace:* dependencies in all three apps.

evals.prompt: Queremos un monorepo para acme con web Next.js, API NestJS, app móvil Expo y una landing en Astro. ¿Cómo lo estructuramos y qué compartimos?
evals.expected_output: The agent recommends openapi mode (because there is a mobile app) and scaffold-monorepo.mjs --scope acme --contracts openapi --apps web,api,mobile,landing, plus a universal design-tokens package for Tailwind/NativeWind. It explains the per-platform isolation rule (ui-web is never imported in mobile; contracts/design-tokens are universal), how to configure metro.config.js and .npmrc for Expo + pnpm, and that apps/landing follows astro-architecture. The reply is in Spanish.
assertions: Recommends openapi mode because of the mobile app
Mentions metro.config.js and .npmrc for Expo + pnpm

evals.prompt: To save time, I imported @acme/ui-web inside apps/mobile and also imported an entity from apps/api into apps/landing/src/pages/index.astro. What does check-boundaries detect?
evals.expected_output: The agent explains that check-boundaries.mjs analyzes both TS/JS files and the frontmatter of .astro files and will report platform-mismatch (native cannot import web) and relative-escape or app-import (no workspace may import apps/api). It proposes moving agnostic tokens to packages/design-tokens, using @acme/api-client or @acme/contracts in landing, and verifying with pnpm check:boundaries.

evals.prompt: We need to add a Node.js worker and a Python FastAPI microservice to the existing monorepo. How do we integrate them?
evals.expected_output: The agent uses scaffold-app.mjs with --type worker (in apps/worker, using @acme/tsconfig/node.json and the node platform) and --type polyglot (in services/<name> with a shim package.json and services/* in pnpm-workspace.yaml, sharing contracts through OpenAPI), running --dry-run first.
